# Rating

Header: `winui/ui/input/Rating.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/Rating.hpp`.

A row of stars the user rates with a click, a drag or the keyboard.

[`value()`](#value) is unset until something is rated, then a number in [1, [`max_rating()`](#max_rating)]. Interaction always commits a whole number, and a click or drag commits only on release (the stars preview the pointer meanwhile; dragging off the left edge and releasing clears). Clicking the star that already is the rating clears it while [`is_clear_enabled()`](#is_clear_enabled). A fractional value set by the app is drawn as a clipped partial star, and a [`placeholder_value()`](#placeholder_value) (say, the average of other users' ratings) is shown while the user has not rated. [`set_read_only()`](#set_read_only) stops user input but keeps the full-strength look and the tab stop. [`ui::Rating`](#uirating) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> stars;

window.set_content(ui::Rating{
    .value             = stars,
    .placeholder_value = 3.5,            // the community average, until the user rates
    .caption           = "312 ratings",
    .horizontal_alignment           = ui::Alignment::Leading,
    // stars is unset again when cleared
});

// Imperatively, a read-only average:
auto average = std::make_unique<ui::RatingControl>(/*max_rating=*/5, /*value=*/4.5);
average->set_read_only(true);
average->set_caption("4.5 average");
```

## `ui::Rating`

A star rating. Builds a [ui::RatingControl](#uiratingcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> stars{3.0};

window.set_content(ui::Rating{
    .value                = stars,
    .caption              = "312 ratings",
    .horizontal_alignment = ui::Alignment::Leading,
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Rating{
    .header, .value, .max_rating, .placeholder_value, .clear_enabled, .initial_set_value,
    .caption, .read_only, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .enabled, .accessibility, .on_value_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited,
    .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

## `ui::RatingControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::RangeValueProvider`.

A row of stars the user rates with a click, a drag or the keyboard.

[`value()`](#value) is unset until something is rated, then a number in [1, [`max_rating()`](#max_rating)]. Interaction always commits a whole number, and a click or drag commits only on release (the stars preview the pointer meanwhile; dragging off the left edge and releasing clears). Clicking the star that already is the rating clears it while [`is_clear_enabled()`](#is_clear_enabled). A fractional value set by the app is drawn as a clipped partial star, and a [`placeholder_value()`](#placeholder_value) (say, the average of other users' ratings) is shown while the user has not rated. [`set_read_only()`](#set_read_only) stops user input but keeps the full-strength look and the tab stop. [`ui::Rating`](#uirating) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> stars;

window.set_content(ui::Rating{
    .value             = stars,
    .placeholder_value = 3.5,            // the community average, until the user rates
    .caption           = "312 ratings",
    .horizontal_alignment           = ui::Alignment::Leading,
    // stars is unset again when cleared
});

// Imperatively, a read-only average:
auto average = std::make_unique<ui::RatingControl>(/*max_rating=*/5, /*value=*/4.5);
average->set_read_only(true);
average->set_caption("4.5 average");
```

### RatingControl

```cpp
RatingControl(std::size_t max_rating = 5, std::optional<double> value = std::nullopt)
```

A row of [`max_rating`](#max_rating) stars (at least 1) holding [`value`](#value), coerced like [`set_value()`](#set_value).

### max_rating

```cpp
std::size_t max_rating() const
```

The number of stars; 5 by default.

### set_max_rating

```cpp
void set_max_rating(std::size_t max_rating)
```

Clamped to >= 1. Re-clamps [value()](#value)/placeholder_value() into the new range, firing [on_value_changed()](#on_value_changed) only if that moves [value()](#value).

### value

```cpp
std::optional<double> value() const
```

Unset until rated, otherwise a value in [1, [max_rating()](#max_rating)] (interaction always lands on a whole number within that range; a fraction is reachable only via [set_value()](#set_value)).

### set_value

```cpp
void set_value(std::optional<double> value)
```

Sets or clears the rating. A value up to 1 rounds up to 1.0, anything above [max_rating()](#max_rating) clamps down to it. Does nothing, and fires no callback, if the result is the current value.

### placeholder_value

```cpp
std::optional<double> placeholder_value() const
```

Unset by default. A grayed preview, such as an average rating, shown only while [value()](#value) is unset and the pointer is not over the control.

### set_placeholder_value

```cpp
void set_placeholder_value(std::optional<double> value)
```

Clamped to [0, [max_rating()](#max_rating)], keeping 0 and fractions below 1 as they are, since a placeholder is a display hint. No-op if unchanged; never fires on_value_changed.

### is_clear_enabled

```cpp
bool is_clear_enabled() const
```

Whether clicking the current rating's star clears it; true by default.

### set_clear_enabled

```cpp
void set_clear_enabled(bool enabled)
```

Whether clicking the star already representing the current rating clears it (default: true).

### initial_set_value

```cpp
int initial_set_value() const
```

Where a keyboard step lands from an unset value; 1 by default.

### set_initial_set_value

```cpp
void set_initial_set_value(int value)
```

The rating a keyboard/gamepad step lands on when stepping from an unset [value()](#value) (default: 1). Clamped to >= 1.

### header

```cpp
const std::string& header() const
```

The label above the stars; empty by default.

### set_header

```cpp
void set_header(std::string header)
```

A label above the stars, which also names the control for screen readers when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Empty (the default) takes no room.

### caption

```cpp
const std::string& caption() const
```

The label right of the stars; empty by default.

### set_caption

```cpp
void set_caption(std::string caption)
```

A decorative label shown to the right of the stars. No interaction reads it. Empty (the default) draws no caption and reserves no width for one.

### read_only

```cpp
bool read_only() const
```

Whether user input is ignored; false by default. Independent of [`enabled()`](../tree/element.md#enabled).

### set_read_only

```cpp
void set_read_only(bool read_only)
```

Ignores pointer and keyboard input while keeping the enabled look and the tab stop, so a screen reader still reaches the rating. [set_value()](#set_value) still works. Turning it on drops any hover or drag preview in progress.

### on_value_changed

```cpp
void on_value_changed(Callback<void(std::optional<double>)> handler)
```

Fired whenever [value()](#value) changes: a click/drag release, a keyboard step, or [set_value()](#set_value) alike, including clearing it (unset).

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the control has keyboard focus.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

A tab stop while enabled, read-only or not.

### hovered

```cpp
bool hovered() const
```

Whether the pointer is over the control, which shows the hover preview.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Custom, with a range value, since UI Automation has no rating role. An unset rating reports 0, because a range value cannot be unset.

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp
std::string automation_name_fallback() const override
```

The header names the control when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name does not.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

A fixed-size row: [max_rating()](#max_rating) star-sized cells plus ([max_rating()](#max_rating) - 1) item-spacing gaps between them, plus [caption()](#caption)'s measured width and a 4 DIP gap when non-empty. [value()](#value) and hover never change it. The header, when set, sits above the row.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Takes the header off the top, leaving [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) as the row of stars.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Hover and drag update the preview; a left-button release commits the star under the pointer (clamped, so releasing past the left edge clears). Ignored while read-only.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the outline stars, the filled (possibly partial) stars for the preview, value or placeholder, the caption and the focus ring.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Marks the control for redraw (the focus ring).

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Up/Right add a star and Down/Left remove one (from an unset value, the first step lands on [`initial_set_value()`](#initial_set_value)); Home goes to 0 (clearing, or 1 when clearing is disabled) and End to [`max_rating()`](#max_rating). Ignored while read-only.
